problem: score_area_for_finding (src/output/json/helpers.rs) buckets a finding into a report area (Forms, Images / alternative text, etc.) via keyword matching over rule_id + title + description. Several WCAG rules embed the raw, page-controlled CSS selector directly into their finding message (e.g. text_spacing.rs's "Content is clipped by '{selector}' ..."), and a selector's class/id name can start with an unrelated area keyword by coincidence (e.g. a class named "alt-service-hero-card" has nothing to do with image alt text) -- word-boundary matching alone doesn't rule this out, since a hyphen is itself a word boundary and "alt-service-hero-card" tokenizes with "alt" as its own leading token.
evidence: Originally found by the report-critic skill's dry-run eval against reports/casoon-batch-en301549.json: summary.accessibility_score_breakdown[] listed area="Images / alternative text" with main_driver="Content clipped when text spacing is increased (1 occurrences)" (routed via "alt" inside the selector "div.alt-service-hero-card" embedded in the a11y.text_spacing.clipped message) — that area has no real image/alt-text violation anywhere in top_recurring_rules. Not reproduced in the 2026-08-31 single-report corpus (casoon.de, satower-mosterei.de, sauerstoffzentrum-nordost.de, shop.satower-mosterei.de, säfte.com), but the underlying selector-embedding pattern is also present in focus_not_obscured_minimum.rs and info_relationships.rs, so it can recur with different selector class names. The sibling "conformance"-contains-"form" and NavigationInteraction-subcategory-leak instances of this same bug class are both fixed; see score-area-form-conformance-word-boundary-misclassification and score-area-navigation-subcategory-misclassification.
expected: A CSS-selector-shaped span (a `.class`/`#id` chain glued directly onto a preceding word, e.g. "div.alt-service-hero-card") embedded in a finding's description must not contribute tokens to area keyword matching -- English prose never glues a `.`/`#` directly onto a following letter without a space, so that pattern reliably identifies selector syntax rather than legitimate word content.
counter_examples: A finding whose rule_id/title/description genuinely mention alt text without any embedded selector (e.g. a11y.alt_text.missing, "Image is missing alternative text.") must still classify into "Images / alternative text"; see score_area_for_finding_still_classifies_real_alt_text_findings.

A finding whose rule_id is genuinely forms-related (e.g. a label-association WCAG rule) must still classify into "Forms" once the fix lands — this is about false positives from incidental substrings, not about removing forms-classification entirely.
